95  Dataset metadata were accessed on 10 October 2026, and the selected EEG recordings and

 96  accompanying metadata were retrieved on 11 October 2026. This secondary analysis used the

 97  released coded participant identifiers; no participants were contacted and no re-identification was

 98  attempted. The author had no access to information that could identify individual participants

 99  during or after data collection. Original collection approval and consent and the regulatory basis

100  for this secondary analysis are documented separately in S2 Text.


101  Analysis windows and chronological partition


102 The derivative contains 18 participant identifiers, six sessions and 360 EDF recordings. Of 7,200

103  exported left/right events, 7,156 provided complete five-second windows. The remaining 44

104  reached the recording boundary before five seconds and were excluded without padding. All 44

105  occurred at the last event of an online recording.


106 The analyzed windows began at the exported class annotation. The original codebook assigns

107  769/770 to left/right cues and 7691/7701 to task starts [16]. The documented MOABB adapter

108 maps the cue codes to a [0,5]-second interval [17]. This establishes the cue-anchored convention

109  used to interpret the released windows. The original task included a 1.5-second cue before

110  feedback, with a five-second offline task period and up to seven seconds of online feedback.

111  Accordingly, the analysis endpoint is task-label decoding over the released cue windows. S1

112  Text, S7 documents the source event definitions, acquisition schedule and subsequent event

113  mapping.
